summary: SpaceX conducted an early-morning launch from California to deliver classified U.S. Space Force spy satellites into orbit, while Chief Executive Elon Musk announced the company will retire the first Starship upper stage successfully caught by launch tower recovery arms. In international space exploration, the joint European-Japanese BepiColombo mission arrived in orbit around Mercury, becoming only the second mission in history to achieve orbit around the innermost planet. On the defense front, the Department of the Air Force is fast-tracking its Space Data Network to secure Joint Force connectivity, as the U.S. Senate prepares to investigate Ukraine’s access to SpaceX's Starshield system, and Canada’s defense minister reported no changes to bilateral defense relations despite a Hegseth memo. In astronomical research, preliminary data from the James Webb Space Telescope identified a possible early-universe black hole that grew faster than its host galaxy, researchers completed a record-resolution Milky Way simulation using three supercomputers, and NASA's Fermi mission published a 14-year all-sky map bridging astronomy's elusive "MeV gap." Looking ahead, readers should watch on Nov. 23 as Amazon is scheduled to launch its first batch of internet satellites since a previous Vulcan Centaur failure.
